item.title: PRS for Music CEO Andrea Czapary Martin to step down in 2026
item.description: British music rights management organisation PRS for Music has confirmed that its chief executive, Andrea Czapary Martin, will step down from her role at the end of 2026. The organisation announced on 5 March that the decision was made in agreement with the PRS Members’ Council to allow for an orderly leadership transition and ensure continuity for the society and its members. item.title: SA: DJ Stokie shares new single Amazwe
item.description: South African amapiano producer and DJ Stokie has released a new single titled ‘Amazwe’, featuring Zain SA, DJ Nana and Neo Soul. The track brings together several South African artists in a collaboration that blends vocal performances with amapiano production. The title ‘Amazwe’, which translates to “nations”, reflects themes of identity, gratitude and life experiences. item.title: Shoday named Apple Music’s Africa Rising Cover Star
item.description: Apple Music has named Nigerian Afrobeats artist Shoday as the latest cover star of its Africa Rising programme, highlighting emerging artists from across the continent. The announcement places the singer on the cover of the Africa Rising playlist, a platform created by Apple Music to promote developing African talent to global audiences. item.title: Nigeria: Ayra Starr releases new single Where Do We Go
item.description: Nigerian Afropop singer Ayra Starr has released a new single titled ‘Where Do We Go’, marking her first release of the year. The track, issued through Mavin Records, was produced by ILY​A and blends Afropop rhythms with upbeat percussion and bass-driven instrumentation. item.title: Angélique Kidjo announces new album HOPE!! ft. global collaborations
item.description: Five-time Grammy Award-winning singer Angélique Kidjo has announced a new album titled HOPE!!, a project that brings together artists and producers from across Africa, Europe and the Americas. The record, set to be out on 24 April, was recorded in Paris and Los Angeles over three years. item.title: Deezer expands Women Chart to six new countries on anniversary
item.description: Music streaming platform Deezer has expanded its Women Chart to six additional countries as it marks the initiative’s first anniversary, coinciding with International Women's Day. The chart, launched in March 2025, tracks the 50 most-streamed songs by female artists each month. It was initially rolled out in markets including France, Germany, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Mexico. The company said the chart will now also be available in Serbia, Bulgaria, the Netherlands, Denmark, Croatia

item.title: Streaming platforms introduce policies to manage AI-generated music
item.description: Major music streaming platforms have introduced a range of policies to address the growing presence of artificial intelligence (AI) in music creation and distribution. As AI tools become increasingly common in the music industry, streaming services have begun implementing rules governing how AI-generated or AI-assisted content is handled on their platforms. item.title: Sony Music West Africa to host Bloom and Bloom events for International Women’s Day
item.description: Sony Music Entertainment’s West Africa division has announced the return of its Women’s Month initiative, Bloom & Bloom, as part of activities marking International Women's Day 2026. The programme aims to highlight the contributions of women across Africa’s creative and business sectors and will feature a series of discussions and networking events focused on collaboration, mentorship and leadership. item.title: Zian SZ: The Zambian rapper bringing Zamrok into a new generation
item.description: By Sibongile Kobo, Tshifhiwa Tendani and Axolile Lucky Mke Zambian rapper Zian SZ is part of a new wave of artists drawing attention to the evolving Zamrok sound. Blending rap with elements rooted in Zambia’s musical heritage, the 21-year-old artist is using her music to explore identity, culture and social issues. item.title: Kelly Khumalo, Amanda Black and Simmy to perform at Durban festival
item.description: South African singers Kelly Khumalo, Amanda Black and Simmy are scheduled to perform at the upcoming She’s Power Fest, which will take place on 28 March at Munies Hockey Club in Durban. The event, organised by Doek on Fleek Lifestyle Events, is part of a broader initiative known as She’s Power, a platform aimed at highlighting women’s empowerment and celebrating women’s achievements.
